title: Summit Tiles: compact per-route & per-model performance tiles for Console overview
creator: Maya Ortiz
description:
Problem: Customers need a dense, scannable Console view that surfaces per-route and per-model health and unit economics without jumping into a full route detail panel.

Goal: Design a reusable, responsive 'Summit Tile' component set that can be tiled in lists or grids and works at both per-route and per-model scopes. Each tile should: show current latency (p50/p95), throughput (req/s), token metrics (input/output tokens per request, tokens/sec), and a micro-cost indicator (cost per 1k tokens + change). Tiles must support quick interactions: expand for a 12h/24h mini-chart, pin for alerts, and quick actions (open traces, compare model variants, create a rollout).

Deliverables: 1) Pixel-specs for 3 density modes (compact, default, expanded), 2) chart spec for embedded micro-sparklines and mini-waterfall, 3) interaction spec (hover/focus states, keyboard nav, accessibility), 4) annotated Figma frames and dev tokens for spacing/typography, 5) acceptance criteria for PM/Eng handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Tiles render correctly in list and grid at three density breakpoints with no horizontal scroll on standard 1280px Console width
Micro-sparkline chart uses same color scheme as route health palette, supports p50 overlay and hover tooltip with exact P50/P95 numeric values
Cost micro-indicator shows current cost per 1k tokens and percentage delta vs 24h baseline; clicking opens cost-breakdown flyout
Quick actions in the tile (Open traces, Compare variants, Start rollout) are keyboard accessible and fire console APIs described in handoff doc
Tiles are responsive and maintain target data density at 10 tiles per viewport in compact mode without losing primary metrics
chart_specs: Micro-sparkline: SVG path with fixed-height 28px, width 120px. Data: 1 point per 5 minutes for 12h (144 points). Interpolation: monotoneX. Overlays: p50 as dashed line. Tooltip: timestamp + numeric value displayed when hovered.
Mini-waterfall snippet: stacked bar showing percentile token latency contributions (tokenization, attention, kernel, IO). Height 36px, segmented colors mapped to runtime breakdown palette.
Throughput bar: single mini bar with numeric QPS. If sample variance >20% show variance marker (thin shaded band).
Cost delta spark: small numeric delta with caret (green up / red down) and accessible aria-label describing percent change vs baseline.
design_decisions: Use 3 density modes instead of continuous scaling to simplify dev effort and ensure alignment with Console card grids
Prefer monotoneX sparkline to avoid overshoot in tight-height charts; full chart available in expanded panel
Put cost delta near tokens metric to emphasize unit economics coupling with token throughput
Expose only 3 quick actions in primary tile to avoid clutter; additional actions live in expanded controls
